exposure: migrant group (based on region of birth)
outcome: poor diabetes outcomes (including weekly income, comorbidities, need for assistance with core activities, education level, English proficiency, duration of stay in Australia)
cohort: The study included all people aged 30 years and older from the Australian 2021 census data.
finding: Migrants from South-East Asia, North Africa and the Middle East, Southern and Central Asia, and Oceania showed a higher age-standardised prevalence of diabetes compared to the Australian-born population, with distinct socioeconomic and health characteristics associated with poor diabetes outcomes across different migrant groups.
